## This was generated by Fable 5 and exists purely as a diagnostic tool

# Classifier Run Visualizer

A web-based tool for stepping through a `pdf_classifier_core` run: every
inference (with its full four-tier constraint pipeline), override, classify /
extract result, error, deferral probe, and backfill becomes a discrete step you
can scrub through while a page strip shows the document's classification state
evolving over time.

It works purely from the **tracing logs** the core crate already emits
(`tracing-tree` hierarchical output on stderr) — no changes to the classifier
itself.

## Quick start

```bash
cd tools/visualizer
python server.py            # → http://127.0.0.1:7878
```

Then either:

- **live run…** — the server launches `target/debug/pdf_classifier_core.exe`
  for you, acting as the TCP frontend the binary requires
  (`CLASSIFIER_OUTPUT_PORT`), and streams the trace log *and the extraction
  payloads* into the UI as they happen. Requires the workspace to be built.
- **open log / paste** — load a previously captured log. Capture one with:

  ```powershell
  $env:CLASSIFIER_OUTPUT_PORT = <port with a listener>   # binary refuses to start without a frontend
  .\target\debug\pdf_classifier_core.exe -s 44 -e 120 -t 4 -p data\large_test_doc.pdf -l trace 2> run.log
  ```

  The trace goes to **stderr**; the final `page -> class` structure goes to
  stdout and may be appended to the same file (the parser picks both up).
- **sample** — a bundled real run over pages 44–60 of the test document,
  featuring a committed stretch, an override stream, two classification
  mismatches, a deferral with anchor search, and a pair backfill.

`server.py` is stdlib-only Python; the UI is self-contained HTML/JS/CSS (no
CDN), so `index.html` also works opened straight from disk for file/paste mode.

## What you see

- **Page strip** — one cell per page, colored by its currently-decided class.
  Underlines mark ground-truth verdicts (green = classify confirmed, red =
  mismatch), an orange corner marks a failed extraction, dashed outlines are
  in-flight deferral probes, and hatched bands below mark regions that were
  recovered via deferral. Click a cell to jump to the next step touching it.
- **Steps pane** — the run as a sequence of semantic actions grouped by
  classifier-loop iteration (committed / deferral / override-stream). Enable
  *micro-steps* in the toolbar to also see job queuing, polling, worker
  assignment and page-cursor movements.
- **Detail pane** — for an inference step: candidates, Tier 1 definitive
  hits, Tier 2 hard-filter eliminations (with the constraint's own FAIL
  explanation), Tier 3 soft scores ranked with totals, the winner, and the
  Tier 4 override evaluation as its own following step. Deferral steps explain
  probes, guaranteed failures, the anchor, and the chosen backfill strategy.
- **Tree tab** — the document as a literal walkable tree, built from the
  replayed state at the current step (so it grows and re-shapes as you scrub).
  Anchor (organizational) pages are containers; blank (`unknown`) and
  never-decided pages appear as explicit leaves so adjacent anchors always read
  correctly. Deferral anchors carry a ⚓ badge — click it to unfold the
  *failure branches*: every probe tried before that anchor was found (with the
  classifier's own failure reason), the guaranteed-failure records, and the
  backrolled region with each page's before → after class. Pages re-decided by
  a backfill get a ↺ badge with their decision history.
- **Margins tab** — an inference-quality diagnostic: winner-minus-runner-up
  soft-score margin per inference, colored by eventual ground truth (confirmed
  / mismatched / never validated), with definitive-constraint hits shown as
  dots. Low bars that are also red are the soft-constraint tuning targets;
  summary tiles compare average margin overall vs. on wrong inferences.
- **State / errors / extractions / final tabs** — the replayed
  `Context` (decided pages, verdicts, guarantee failures, jobs in flight,
  current parent), every error with jump links, extraction payloads (live runs
  only), and the final structure compared against the replayed state.
- **Error % tab** — the run's final decisions (stdout structure when present,
  else the replayed end state) compared page-by-page against a per-page ground
  truth for `data/large_test_doc.pdf`: overall error rate, per-true-class
  breakdown with confusion counts, and every misclassified page with jump
  links. The ground truth lives in `static/groundtruth.js`, generated by
  `build_groundtruth.py`: the static-classifier export
  (`data/large_test_doc_classified/`) supplies the authoritative
  chapter/subchapter *sequence* (it has no page numbers, and its data-block
  page counts are incomplete), and the PDF's own text signatures position
  every page (`CHAPTER x-y[-z]` headings for anchors, `DMC`/`NATO stock`
  headers for tables, `Fig N:` captions for diagrams, the record-of-mods
  blank after each chapter). Anchor detections are sequence-aligned to the
  export, so OCR-mangled numbers inherit their canonical labels; the
  generator aborts if any export anchor cannot be positioned. Regenerate with
  `python build_groundtruth.py` (needs `pymupdf`) if the export or page range
  changes.
- **Raw log** — the underlying trace lines, synced both ways with the current
  step.

Keyboard: `←`/`→` step, `Shift+←`/`→` iteration, `Space` play/pause,
`Home`/`End` first/last.

## Layout

```
server.py            stdlib HTTP server: static UI + /api/run + SSE + extraction frontend
static/parser.js     tracing-tree text → span/event tree (format notes in the header)
static/model.js      tree → semantic actions with replayable state effects
static/app.js        UI: strip, stepper, detail cards, playback, live-run client
static/index.html    single page
static/style.css     dark/light themes
sample/              a real captured run for the "sample" button
```

## Notes / limitations

- The parser targets the exact subscriber configured in `main.rs`
  (`HierarchicalLayer::new(4)`, no timestamps/targets). Run with `-l trace`
  for full pipeline detail; `info` still yields the major beats.
- ANSI colors are stripped, but capture with a redirected (non-terminal)
  stderr when possible.
- Extraction payload *contents* only exist in live-run mode (the visualizer is
  the streaming frontend); file-mode logs still show extraction ok/fail per
  page.
- The server binds `127.0.0.1` only, and live runs execute the repo's
  classifier binary — it's a local dev tool, not something to expose.
